description: NDT in Maracaibo, Venezuela: inspection for Lake Maracaibo wells, flowlines, tanks and plants as output recovers. Corrosion, methods, radiation rules, hiring.
quickAnswer: Maracaibo is the capital of Venezuela's oldest oil region. More than 30 billion barrels have been produced from the 25,000-square-mile Maracaibo Basin, and over 10,000 oil installations sit around the lake [1]. After years of deferred maintenance, Venezuelan output recovered to about **1.21 million barrels a day in July 2026** [2], and operators are reactivating old wells and replacing corroded lines. One program alone has laid **1,149 km of new flexible pipe** on the lake's eastern shore [3]. That makes Maracaibo one of the largest **integrity recovery** markets in the Americas. Radiological protection is overseen by the **Ministry of Health**, and the **Dirección de Energía Atómica** controls legal import of radiation equipment [4].

sections.h2: Why Maracaibo is a major integrity recovery market
paragraphs: Commercial oil under Lake Maracaibo was identified by 1928, and over a century of production has left more than 10,000 oil installations and thousands of miles of pipelines crisscrossing the lake [1]. Much of this infrastructure is old, and analysts have described it as rundown and leaking, with corroded pipelines, tanks and wellheads responsible for chronic spills [1][5].

That history is now driving a large maintenance and rehabilitation effort. Venezuela's output has been recovering through 2026: PDVSA and its partners averaged 1.21 million barrels a day in July, up from 1.19 million in June [2]. Chevron expects to grow its Venezuelan production by as much as 50% by late 2028, funded by cash flows from its existing joint ventures [2], and has said its three ventures are on track to reach about 300,000 barrels a day of gross production by the end of 2026 [6]. Rigs that have been idle for years are being inspected and refurbished, and some are going to shipyards in Trinidad and Guyana for inspection before returning to work [7].

For NDT providers, this means sustained demand for well integrity support, flowline and pipeline inspection, tank and terminal assessment, and inspection of refurbished drilling and production equipment. Restoring what already exists is the quickest path to more production, which puts inspection at the center of the recovery [8].

sections.h2: Assets and inspection scopes around the lake
paragraphs: Lake Maracaibo production combines thousands of shallow-water wells on platforms and piles, subsea and surface flowlines, flow stations, gas compression plants, storage terminals and crude ports. Onshore, the eastern shore towns of Cabimas, Lagunillas and Bachaquero host fields, workshops and logistics bases, while Maracaibo city provides engineering, supply and services.

paragraphs: Lake Maracaibo is brackish, warm and biologically active, and much of its infrastructure dates back decades. Steel lines and structures suffer internal corrosion from water and CO2 in production fluids, microbiologically influenced corrosion, and external corrosion in the splash zone and at the waterline. Well integrity specialists point to tubing and casing corrosion driven by high water cut and CO2 exposure as a key challenge in reactivating mature wells [9].

Operators are tackling the problem in two ways: replacing worst-affected lines and inspecting the rest to decide what can stay in service. North American Blue Energy Partners has replaced aging steel lines with flexible pipe laid from barges in continuous sections, which leaves fewer joints where leaks usually start [3]. Its program has run new flowlines and gas lines to 435 wells in the Bachaquero and Ceuta fields [3].

For lines that remain steel, NDT is used to map wall loss, find localized pitting and decide on repair, sleeve or replacement. Guided wave UT can screen long sections from a single location, and corrosion mapping and spot UT then quantify the worst areas.

Reactivating mature wells is one of the fastest ways to add production, but it starts with integrity checks. Specialists highlight sustained casing pressure, cement degradation, packer failures, sand production and wellhead degradation as common problems, with solutions that include ultrasonic cement logs, pressure testing and NDT of surface equipment [9][10].

NDT crews support this work by inspecting wellheads, valves and surface piping for corrosion and erosion, checking threaded connections and flanges, verifying repair welds, and inspecting artificial lift equipment and pump components. Downhole logging is a specialist field, but surface integrity inspection is a core NDT scope.

**Ultrasonic thickness testing** is the most widely used method, for flowlines, tanks, vessels and structures. **Corrosion mapping** with manual or automated scanners gives detailed wall-loss pictures for engineering assessment. **Guided wave UT** screens long pipe runs, including those partially submerged or buried.

**Radiography** is used for weld inspection on repairs and new construction, and profile radiography can show wall loss in small-bore lines. **Magnetic particle** and **penetrant** inspection check welds, structural members and refurbished equipment for cracks. **MFL floor scanning** inspects storage tank floors, and **visual inspection** by qualified inspectors remains essential for platforms and structures, often using rope access or boats.
For refurbished rigs and cranes, MT and UT of critical structural welds, pins and lifting points support recertification before return to service.

sections.h2: Radiation protection and radiography rules in Venezuela
paragraphs: Industrial gamma radiography is widely used in Venezuela, mainly with iridium-192 sources. A paper by the Dirección General de Energía Atómica reported 62 authorized companies providing industrial gammagraphy services, with 388 cameras in use, and proposed improvements such as individual licensing of occupationally exposed workers [11].

According to Official Gazette No. 38.572, the Ministry of Health's Dirección General de Salud Ambiental y Contraloría Sanitaria is the national competent authority for radiological protection and safety, while the Dirección de Energía Atómica, now under the Ministry of Science and Technology, governs the legal import of radiation equipment [4]. Decree No. 2210 sets technical standards and procedures for handling radioactive materials [12].

Buyers should confirm that radiography providers hold current authorizations, that sources and cameras were legally imported and are properly documented, that operators have radiation protection training, and that transport and storage arrangements meet national requirements.
bullets: Check the provider's current authorizations for industrial gammagraphy [4][11].
Confirm source documentation, transport arrangements and secure storage [12].
Ask for radiation protection training records for every operator.

paragraphs: Venezuelan oil operations have long used international codes alongside national and company standards. Inspection typically follows API standards (API 510, 570 and 653 for in-service equipment, API 1104 for pipeline welding), ASME codes for pressure equipment, and ASNT-based personnel certification. Joint ventures with international partners often apply their own corporate standards and expect ASNT, ISO 9712 or equivalent certification.

Because many technicians left the country during the downturn, buyers should verify certification validity and recent hands-on experience carefully, and consider supervision by experienced Level IIIs for critical scopes.

Lake Maracaibo's pollution is a major public and environmental concern. Analysts estimate cleanup would cost more than $2.5 billion, with oil slicks and algal blooms frequently covering the lake [13]. Leaks from corroded lines and tanks are the main source, which makes integrity inspection directly relevant to environmental performance.

Prioritizing inspection by consequence makes sense: lines near shorelines and communities, tank farms and loading terminals, and high-throughput trunk lines first. Repair verification and leak testing after replacement or sleeving should be documented so operators can show progress.

Maracaibo is hot and humid year-round, which affects equipment and crews. Much lake work is done from boats and barges, with platforms accessed by ladders or rope access, so marine safety, fall protection and water rescue plans are essential. Power outages and fuel shortages have affected operations in the region, so providers should plan for generators, spare batteries and fuel.

Equipment availability can be a constraint: advanced NDT instruments, probes and spares may need to be imported, so providers with established supply chains and in-country stock have an advantage. Security planning for personnel and equipment is also part of operating in the region.

With thousands of installations and limited budgets, operators need data that helps them decide where to spend first. NDT deliverables should tie every reading to a clear asset and location identifier, include photographs and GPS coordinates for lake assets, and grade findings by severity so engineers can rank repairs. Corrosion maps and thickness surveys should be repeatable, so future inspections can measure corrosion rates rather than single snapshots.

Digital reporting also supports transparency with partners and authorities. Joint ventures with international partners often require reporting formats compatible with their integrity management systems, and documented before-and-after inspections help demonstrate progress on leak reduction, which is increasingly important for environmental and community relations.

Restoring Venezuelan production to historic levels is estimated to require up to $100 billion in capital and more than a decade of work [13], which points to long-term demand for inspection. Near-term opportunities include flowline and pipeline condition assessment, tank and terminal inspections, well reactivation support, rig and equipment recertification, and construction NDT on replacement facilities.

International providers can partner with Venezuelan firms that hold local authorizations and know the region, while local companies can grow by investing in advanced methods such as corrosion mapping, guided wave and phased array UT.

sections.h2: How NDT is priced in Maracaibo
paragraphs: NDT is usually priced on day rates per technician and method, with marine transport, rope access and equipment charged separately. Long-term service contracts with joint ventures are common. Imported equipment, logistics and security costs can make rates higher than local labor costs alone would suggest.
NDT-Connect lets buyers post one scope and compare providers serving Maracaibo, the eastern shore and western Venezuela.

The recovery is creating demand for UT, RT, MT and PT technicians, corrosion mapping and guided wave specialists, tank inspectors and Level IIIs. Experienced Venezuelan technicians who worked abroad have valuable skills, and training new technicians is a growing need.
A typical path starts with Level II certification in UT and RT, radiation protection training for radiography roles, and then advanced UT methods and API inspector certifications.

sections.h2: How to choose an NDT provider in Maracaibo
paragraphs: Use this checklist when pre-qualifying providers.
bullets: Verified ASNT, ISO 9712 or equivalent certifications and recent field experience.
Current radiography authorizations and documented sources [4][11].
Marine and rope access capability for lake platforms and lines.
Corrosion mapping, guided wave and tank inspection capability.
Reliable logistics: in-country equipment, spares, power and security planning.
Clear reporting that supports repair and replacement decisions.

faqs.q: Why is NDT demand growing in Maracaibo?
faqs.a: Venezuelan output is recovering, reaching about 1.21 million b/d in July 2026 [2], and operators are reactivating wells and assessing or replacing corroded infrastructure around Lake Maracaibo [1][3].

faqs.q: What are the main damage mechanisms on Lake Maracaibo?
faqs.a: Internal corrosion from water and CO2, microbiologically influenced corrosion, and external splash-zone corrosion on aging steel lines, platforms and tanks [1][9].
The Ministry of Health is the national competent authority for radiological protection, and the Dirección de Energía Atómica controls legal import of radiation equipment [4].

faqs.q: How many companies provide industrial gammagraphy in Venezuela?
faqs.a: A Dirección General de Energía Atómica paper reported 62 authorized companies with 388 gammagraphy cameras [11].

faqs.q: Which NDT methods are most used in Maracaibo?
faqs.a: UT thickness and corrosion mapping, guided wave, radiography, MT and PT, MFL tank floor scanning and visual inspection.

faqs.q: How do I request NDT quotes in Maracaibo?
faqs.a: Post the scope on NDT-Connect with assets, location (lake or onshore), methods, access, dates and reporting requirements.
